PepsiCo is a global food and beverage company founded in 1965, known for brands like Pepsi, Gatorade, and Frito-Lay. It operates in over 200 countries and has a history of steady growth and dividend increases. The company focuses on convenient foods and beverages, aiming for both financial success and positive social impact.

PepsiCo Inc. (PEP) is a leading food and beverage company that manufactures and distributes its products in more than 200 countries. Food products that PepsiCo manufactures include chips, flavored snacks, cereals, rice, pasta, and dairy-based products. The company's beverage product portfolio includes carbonated soft drinks, juices, ready-to-drink tea and coffee, sports drinks, and bottled water. Headquartered in Purchase, New York, the company employs around 274,000 people worldwide. [...] According to Information Resources, Inc. (or IRI), a market research company, PepsiCo owns nine of the 40 largest packaged goods trademarks in the United States. The company owns several brands, and 22 of them, including Pepsi, Lays, and Gatorade, generate more than $1 billion each in revenues.

You can invest in this sector through exchange traded funds (or ETFs) such as the Consumer Staples Select Sector Standard & Poors depositary receipt (or SPDR) Fund (XLP). PepsiCo is also part of other ETFs such as the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG).

PepsiCo, Inc., based in Purchase, New York, is one of the world’s largest food and beverage companies. PepsiCo is known for its Frito-Lay snack food brands, soft drinks under its Gatorade, Mountain Dew, and namesake Pepsi brands, and cereal products under its Quaker Oats subsidiary.

The PepsiCo name is deeply embedded within American pop culture. It emerged in 1965, when the Pepsi-Cola Company merged with Frito-Lay, Inc. [...] From its humble late-19th century roots to its 21st century place as a top global food and beverage conglomerate with a presence in more than 200 countries, PepsiCo has strived to grow its reach through product innovation, strategic acquisition, and dynamic marketing aimed at linking hearts, minds, and taste buds. Although its product lineup skews more toward flavor than nutrition, the company has demonstrated a willingness to adapt its brands to changing—and regional—tastes and preferences. [...] PepsiCo’s business structure includes seven divisions: three in North America and the remaining four in various regions around the world. The company has a history of steady growth and stability, having raised its dividend each year for more than 50 years, making it what’s known as a dividend king. As of 2023, PepsiCo brands—present in over 200 countries—serve over a billion customers each day.

## Founding and early history

PepsiCo is an American multinational food and beverage corporation formed in 1965 through the merger of Pepsi-Cola Company and Frito-Lay. It has since expanded its portfolio through acquisitions and mergers to include brands like Quaker, Tropicana, Gatorade and Frito-Lay. PepsiCo's mission is to produce convenient foods and beverages while delivering financial returns and opportunities for growth. It aims to achieve business success while having a positive social and environmental impact. Varun

PepsiCo offers a wide range of products including Pepsi, Gatorade, Tropicana, Frito-Lay snacks, and Quaker cereals. The company also markets Aquafina water and various beverage brands globally. PepsiCo's product portfolio includes both food and beverages.

PepsiCo's revenue model includes direct sales of beverages, snacks, and nutritional products, strategic partnerships, and acquisitions. Its main revenue streams come from North America beverages and the Frito-Lay segment. PepsiCo also invests in digital sales and direct-to-consumer services.

The revenue model of PepsiCo is multi-faceted, encompassing direct sales, strategic partnerships, and acquisitions. The company generates income through the sale of its extensive product lineup, which includes beverages, snacks, and nutritional products. In addition to traditional retail channels, PepsiCo has made significant investments in digital transformation, enabling online sales and direct-to-consumer delivery services. The company also benefits from its collaboration with franchised [...] with franchised bottlers and distributors who contribute to its wide-reaching market penetration. #### PepsiCo’s Revenue Model

Revenue and income are important metrics when looking at a stock to evaluate its investment potential. Higher numbers translate to higher share prices and increased dividends. PepsiCo's diverse product portfolio has allowed the company to have multiple consistent revenue streams. The two biggest revenue contributors are its North America beverage channel, which contributes around 30%, while the Frito-Lay segment adds about 27%.

PepsiCo's Balanced Approach: Growth, Dividends and Stability [...] In addition, PepsiCo remains attractively priced from a valuation perspective. I believe the stock remains seriously discounted in the market by the current high interest rate environment. As the company experiences accelerating revenue growth, I anticipate an upward re-rating of its price-earnings multiple. With an attractive forward dividend yield of approximately 3.12% and expected earnings per share growth of over 7% in the coming years, the company presents a compelling opportunity for [...] ability to increase revenue even during periods of high inflation, indicating that a mature company like PepsiCo has the pricing power to keep pace with or even exceed the overall inflation rates.

PepsiCo operates through seven global divisions that encompass beverages, snacks, and food. The three largest divisions are PepsiCo Beverages North America, Frito-Lay North America, and Europe. Together these divisions accounted for over 50% of PepsiCo's 2021 revenues. PepsiCo diversifies its revenue streams across product categories and global regions to reduce risk from declines in any single area.
